entries.title: Jadhav (India v Pakistan)
entries.principle: The denial of consular access under the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations engages State responsibility; the appropriate remedy is review and reconsideration of the conviction and sentence.
entries.facts: India claimed that Pakistan violated the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations in the case of Kulbhushan Jadhav.
entries.holding: The denial of consular access under the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations engages State responsibility; the appropriate remedy is review and reconsideration of the conviction and sentence.

entries.title: Actions pour la Protection des Droits de l'Homme (APDH) v Republic of Côte d'Ivoire
entries.court: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: The composition of an electoral commission must be independent and impartial; a commission dominated by the executive violates the right to participate in public affairs.
entries.facts: A challenge to the composition of the electoral commission in Côte d'Ivoire.
entries.holding: The composition of an electoral commission must be independent and impartial; a commission dominated by the executive violates the right to participate in public affairs.
entries.judges: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights

entries.title: Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Croatia v Serbia)
entries.principle: Genocide requires specific intent to destroy a protected group in whole or in part; the failure to prevent or punish genocide engages State responsibility.
entries.facts: Croatia claimed that Serbia was responsible for genocide during the Croatian war of independence.
entries.holding: Genocide requires specific intent to destroy a protected group in whole or in part; the failure to prevent or punish genocide engages State responsibility.

entries.title: Konaté v Burkina Faso
entries.court: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: Criminal defamation with custodial sentences is disproportionate and violates the right to freedom of expression; civil remedies are the appropriate response.
entries.facts: A journalist was convicted of criminal defamation and sentenced to imprisonment.
entries.holding: Criminal defamation with custodial sentences is disproportionate and violates the right to freedom of expression; civil remedies are the appropriate response.
entries.judges: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights

entries.title: Zongo and Others v Burkina Faso
entries.court: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: The State must conduct an effective investigation into the assassination of a journalist; failure to do so violates the right to life and to freedom of expression.
entries.facts: A journalist was assassinated and the State failed to investigate.
entries.holding: The State must conduct an effective investigation into the assassination of a journalist; failure to do so violates the right to life and to freedom of expression.
entries.judges: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights

entries.title: Tanganyika Law Society and Legal and Human Rights Centre v United Republic of Tanzania
entries.court: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: Restrictions on the right to freedom of expression must be prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society; vague or overbroad laws fail the legality test.

entries.title: Ahmadou Sadio Diallo (Republic of Guinea v Democratic Republic of the Congo)
entries.principle: The arbitrary arrest, detention and expulsion of an alien engages State responsibility; reparation includes compensation for material and moral damage.
entries.facts: Guinea claimed that the DRC arbitrarily arrested, detained and expelled a Guinean national.
entries.holding: The arbitrary arrest, detention and expulsion of an alien engages State responsibility; reparation includes compensation for material and moral damage.

entries.title: Good v Botswana
entries.court: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: The death penalty must be imposed only after a fair trial with all guarantees; States must ensure that the convicted person has exhausted all remedies.

entries.title: Centre for Minority Rights Development (Kenya) and Minority Rights Group International on behalf of Endorois Welfare Council v Kenya
entries.court: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: The eviction of an indigenous community from its ancestral land without consent or compensation violates the rights to property, culture, religion and natural resources under the African Charter.
entries.facts: The Endorois community was evicted from its ancestral land in the Lake Bogoria area.
entries.holding: The eviction of an indigenous community from its ancestral land without consent or compensation violates the rights to property, culture, religion and natural resources under the African Charter.
entries.judges: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights

entries.title: Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Bosnia and Herzegovina v Serbia and Montenegro)
entries.principle: A State is responsible for genocide where it commits, or is complicit in, acts of genocide; the duty to prevent and punish genocide is an obligation of conduct, not result.
entries.facts: Bosnia and Herzegovina claimed that Serbia was responsible for genocide during the Bosnian war.
entries.holding: A State is responsible for genocide where it commits, or is complicit in, acts of genocide; the duty to prevent and punish genocide is an obligation of conduct, not result.

entries.title: Armed Activities on the Territory of the Congo (Democratic Republic of the Congo v Uganda)
entries.principle: A State is responsible for human-rights violations committed by its armed forces on foreign territory; reparation includes compensation and the obligation to withdraw.
entries.facts: The DRC claimed that Uganda was responsible for human-rights violations on Congolese territory.
entries.holding: A State is responsible for human-rights violations committed by its armed forces on foreign territory; reparation includes compensation and the obligation to withdraw.

entries.title: Avena and Other Mexican Nationals (Mexico v United States of America)
entries.principle: The failure to inform a foreign national of the right to consular assistance under the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations engages State responsibility and requires review and reconsideration.
entries.facts: Mexico claimed that the United States failed to inform Mexican nationals of their right to consular assistance.
entries.holding: The failure to inform a foreign national of the right to consular assistance under the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations engages State responsibility and requires review and reconsideration.

entries.title: Legal Consequences of the Construction of a Wall in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (Advisory Opinion)
entries.principle: The construction of the wall in the Occupied Palestinian Territory is contrary to international law; Israel is under an obligation to cease the works and make reparation.
entries.facts: An advisory opinion on the legal consequences of the construction of a wall in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
entries.holding: The construction of the wall in the Occupied Palestinian Territory is contrary to international law; Israel is under an obligation to cease the works and make reparation.

entries.title: LaGrand (Germany v United States of America)
entries.principle: Provisional measures indicated by the Court under Article 41 of the Statute are binding, and the Court may order measures to preserve rights pending judgment.
entries.facts: Germany claimed that the United States failed to inform two German nationals of their right to consular assistance.
entries.holding: Provisional measures indicated by the Court under Article 41 of the Statute are binding, and the Court may order measures to preserve rights pending judgment.

entries.title: Amnesty International & Others v Zambia
entries.court: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: The detention of journalists and the closure of newspapers violate the right to freedom of expression and to receive information under the Charter.
entries.facts: Journalists were detained and a newspaper was closed.
entries.holding: The detention of journalists and the closure of newspapers violate the right to freedom of expression and to receive information under the Charter.
entries.judges: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights

entries.title: Media Rights Agenda v Nigeria
entries.court: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: The right to freedom of expression is fundamental to the African Charter; restrictions must be prescribed by law, serve a legitimate aim and be necessary and proportionate.

entries.title: Legality of the Threat or Use of Nuclear Weapons (Advisory Opinion)
entries.principle: The threat or use of nuclear weapons would generally be contrary to the rules of international law applicable in armed conflict, and in particular the principles of distinction and proportionality.
entries.facts: An advisory opinion on the legality of the threat or use of nuclear weapons.
entries.holding: The threat or use of nuclear weapons would generally be contrary to the rules of international law applicable in armed conflict, and in particular the principles of distinction and proportionality.

entries.title: Reservations to the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Advisory Opinion)
entries.principle: A reservation must be compatible with the object and purpose of the treaty; the compatibility test is applied by reference to the treaty's aims, not by the reserving State's unilateral view.
entries.facts: An advisory opinion on whether reservations to the Genocide Convention were permissible.
entries.holding: A reservation must be compatible with the object and purpose of the treaty; the compatibility test is applied by reference to the treaty's aims.

entries.title: Factory at Chorzów (Germany v Poland)
entries.principle: Reparation must, as far as possible, wipe out all the consequences of the illegal act and re-establish the situation which would, in all probability, have existed but for it (restitutio in integrum).
entries.facts: Germany claimed reparation for Poland's unlawful expropriation of a nitrate factory.
entries.holding: Reparation must, as far as possible, wipe out all the consequences of the illegal act and re-establish the situation which would, in all probability, have existed but for it (restitutio in integrum).
entries.judges: Huber, President (Permanent Court of International Justice)
